variants.title: GM counting statistics at a low count rate
variants.sample: Weak Cs-137 source, a few counts per second
variants.unknown: whether the scatter is Poisson at a low count rate
variants.note: With a mean of only about 15 counts the Poisson distribution is visibly skewed; the standard deviation is still the square root of the mean.

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, ch. 3: Poisson statistics for a mean of a few counts

variants.title: GM counting statistics at a high count rate
variants.sample: Cs-137 source, a few hundred counts per second
variants.unknown: whether the scatter is Gaussian at a high count rate
variants.note: With a mean of several hundred counts the Poisson distribution is almost exactly a Gaussian of the same standard deviation; dead-time losses are small but not zero.

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, ch. 3: Gaussian limit of the Poisson distribution

variants.title: GM counting statistics of the background alone
variants.sample: No source: natural background (cosmic rays and room radioactivity)
variants.unknown: the scatter of the background counts
variants.note: Background is a count of independent events too, so it scatters as the square root of its mean.

source.title: G. F. Knoll, Radiation Detection and Measurement, ch. 3 and ch. 18: background as a Poisson process
